title: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS) — 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average, 12:00 p.m. ET, surveying 9/24–9/30, the first full post-FOMC-decision window and the week that brackets quarter-end
source: EST: canonical file written by this event's own initial research 2026-09-16, after reading the single proposal carrying this id (proposals/pmms-2026-10-01.from-fhfa-hpi-2026-09-29.json) in full. BOTH of its primaries were RE-FETCHED AND RE-EXTRACTED INDEPENDENTLY THIS SESSION rather than inherited. (1) freddiemac.com/pmms/docs/PMMS_Publication_Calendar.pdf (HTTP 200, 93,314 bytes), the publisher's own forward-dated publication calendar, inflated in-session by a pure-Python FlateDecode pass over its 8 compressed streams (306,198 chars) and text-extracted from the show-text operators: the row reads verbatim "Publication Date 10/1/2026 | Week Beginning 9/24/2026 | Week Ending 9/30/2026", and its neighbours "9/17/2026 | 9/10/2026 | 9/16/2026" and "9/24/2026 | 9/17/2026 | 9/23/2026" reproduce to the day. (2) freddiemac.com/pmms (HTTP 200, 103,786 bytes) states the standing rule verbatim — "PMMS results are released weekly on Thursdays at 12 p.m. ET. and are an average of loan rates offered the prior Thursday through Wednesday" — and carries the live reading the calendar anchors against, "U.S. weekly mortgage rate averages as of 09/10/2026, 30-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage 6.76%, 15-year Fixed-Rate Mortgage 6.09%". So the date is named on the publisher's forward calendar AND derivable from the publisher's stated rule, and the two agree. THE DATE IS NOT IN DOUBT; the estimate label is taxonomy. CONFIRMED_PREFIX in scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs (IR|CAL|BLS|FED|PJM|SEC|TSY|OCC|BEA|CENSUS|ISM|CB|UMICH|FHFA) carries no member for a GSE's own weekly survey, and this lane may not flip a status without an IR:/BLS:/FED: primary. Checked 2026-09-16
notes: WHAT THIS EVENT IS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED (initial research 2026-09-16, full working in docs/research/events/pmms-2026-10-01.md). The PMMS 30-year average is NOT an independent information event: it is a lagged restatement of the 10-year Treasury over its own survey window. Pairing all 36 published 2026 PMMS readings against the average CMT 10Y over each print's stated Thursday-through-Wednesday window (home.treasury.gov daily par yields, fetched direct 2026-09-16, 177 sessions of 2026 + 249 of 2025) gives a primary-secondary spread of mean 1.967pp, sd 0.054pp, and over the last 13 weeks mean 1.987pp with sd 0.019pp — under 2bp of week-to-week dispersion. A purely out-of-sample rule (window-average 10Y + the trailing-13-week mean spread, no peeking) over 75 paired weeks of 2025-2026 lands MAE 6.6bp, 73% within 10bp, and the last six weeks within 3bp each. Its one real failure is a spread REGIME shift, not noise: the 2025 mean was 2.295pp against 2026's 1.967pp, and the four worst errors in the whole sample (19-23bp) are all January-February 2026, the transition itself. SO THE CALL ON THE SERIES, WHICH THE PROPOSING SWEEP EXPLICITLY LEFT OPEN: do NOT backfill PMMS as a weekly calendar series. 52 sessions a year would buy a number already derivable to ~7bp from Treasury data this repo fetches anyway; this edition earns its slot only because its window 9/24-9/30 is the first FULL post-decision week after the 2026-09-16 FOMC and brackets both quarter-end and the 09-30 government-funding deadline, and because it sits inside fhfa-hpi-2026-09-29's own corridor. THE LEVEL IS THE STORY, NOT THE SURPRISE. Measured 2026-09-16: 30-year FRM 6.66 (08-27) -> 6.71 (09-03) -> 6.76 (09-10) against 6.35 a year earlier, +41bp y/y. The 10Y has since run to 5.00 (09-15) from a 4.795 average over the 09-10 print's own window, so ~20bp of mortgage-rate rise is ALREADY BANKED and not yet published. On four of five known days the 09-17 print projects 6.96% (+19bp) — larger than any weekly move of 2026, whose maximum is +0.16pp. At an unchanged 10Y of 5.00 the 10-01 print lands ~6.99%; the 7.00% line has not printed since 2025-01-16 (7.04%), 86 weeks, with a 6.96% post-peak. A 7-handle is a headline threshold for every housing name in the 09-29/09-30 corridor, and it would report a y/y gap near +65bp against 6.34% on 2025-10-02. Impact low and symbols [] are this session's own re-measurement, not inherited: no macro- or housing-keyed playbook exists in docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md or docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-16, 0 hits), and naming a builder here would commit the deterministic screen to probe a ticker whose 5% moves are builder idiosyncratics (KBH prints 09-22) rather than information about a mortgage average. Transmission runs rates -> mortgage -> builders, never the reverse. An estimate widens caution; nothing here licenses an entry.
